title: ServiceNow
description: A ServiceNow instance's tables — incidents, problems, changes, requests, the CMDB, users and groups, knowledge — with each field's label and the table it refers to.

fields.name: instance
fields.label: Instance
fields.help: Paste the address of any page of the instance, or just its name (acme).

fields.name: auth
fields.label: Sign in with
fields.help: basic: the integration user's name and password. oauth: an OAuth application (client credentials), where basic sign-in is turned off.

fields.name: tables
fields.label: Tables to add
fields.help: Tables to read besides the usual ITSM, catalog, CMDB, people and knowledge tables (comma-separated names).

fields.name: displayValue
fields.label: Read display values
fields.help: false (best): raw values — sys_ids, choice values, UTC times — that join and compare exactly. true: what a person sees (names, labels, local times), which cannot be joined on.

setup.title: Where your instance is
setup.say: Paste the address of any page of your ServiceNow instance (acme.service-now.com), or just its name.

fix.say: The instance is asleep. A developer instance hibernates when unused: wake it at developer.servicenow.com (Start building), then check again.

setup.title: A user that may only read
setup.say:
Superatom only reads. Give it an integration user of its own whose roles only read. As an admin, first elevate to security_admin (your name, top right → Elevate role), then:

1. All → User Administration → Users → New. User ID: superatom.integration. First name: Superatom. Tick Web service access only (Internal Integration User, where your release shows it). Time zone: GMT. Submit; open the user again → Set Password → copy it.

2. In the user's Roles list → Edit… → add snc_read_only, itil (incidents, problems, changes, requests, catalog tasks, users and groups), cmdb_read (the CMDB) and knowledge (knowledge articles) → Save. snc_read_only keeps every role the user has from changing anything.

Where basic sign-in is turned off, use OAuth (client credentials, Washington DC or later): System Properties → set glide.oauth.inbound.client.credential.grant_type.enabled to true; then System OAuth → Application Registry → New → Create an OAuth API endpoint for external clients. Name: Superatom. Default Grant type: Client Credentials. OAuth Application User: the integration user above. Submit, open it again, and copy its Client ID and Client Secret here.

fix.say: ServiceNow refused that user ID or password. Check both (User ID, not the name), that the user is Active and not locked out, and set its password again if unsure.

ServiceNow refused the OAuth application. Check its Client ID and Client Secret, that its Default Grant type is Client Credentials with an OAuth Application User, and that glide.oauth.inbound.client.credential.grant_type.enabled is true.
Signed in, but the user may not read users. Give it the itil role (and snc_read_only), as above.

setup.title: Which tables
setup.say: Superatom reads incident, problem, change_request, change_task, sc_request, sc_req_item, sc_task, task, task_sla, cmdb_ci, cmdb_ci_server, cmdb_rel_ci, sys_user, sys_user_group, sys_user_grmember, cmn_location, cmn_department, core_company and kb_knowledge. Name any others to read too (u_vendor). Values are read raw — sys_ids, choice values and UTC times, which join and compare exactly — unless you choose display values. The check reads a row of each table.

fix.say: The user may not read how tables are described (sys_dictionary, sys_db_object). Add the personalize_dictionary role to it — snc_read_only keeps it from changing anything — then check again.
That table is not on this instance, or the user may not see it. Use its name, not its label (System Definition → Tables shows both).

fix.when: may read none of the tables|User Not Authorized|not allowed
fix.say: The user may not read those tables. Give it the role each needs (itil for ITSM tables, cmdb_read for the CMDB, knowledge for articles; a custom table's own read role), then check again.
